landmarks.name: Sultan Omar Ali Saifuddien Mosque
landmarks.writeup: A stunning mosque in Bandar Seri Begawan, known for its golden dome and beautiful lagoon.

wiki.extract: Omar Ali Saifuddien III Sa'adul Khairi Waddien reigned as the Sultan of Brunei from 1950 until his abdication in 1967.

landmarks.name: Ulu Temburong National Park
landmarks.writeup: A pristine rainforest park offering canopy walks and rich biodiversity.

wiki.extract: Ulu Temburong National Park is the first national park to be established in Brunei, protected since 1991. The park is in Temburong District in eastern Brunei, and covers about 40% of the district in the south at 550 square kilometres (210 sq mi). It is within the Batu Apoi Forest Reserve. The park contains unspoiled jungle and is known as the "Green Jewel of Brunei", described as "the finest example of the sultanate's successful forest protection policy". The principal rivers are the Temburong and Belalong Rivers. It is an important ecotourism centre in Brunei and hosts the Ulu Ulu Resort. The Peradayan Forest Reserve is also located in the district.

landmarks.name: Istana Nurul Iman
landmarks.writeup: The official residence of the Sultan of Brunei, one of the largest residential palaces in the world.

wiki.extract: The Istana Nurul Iman is the official residence of the Sultan of Brunei, Hassanal Bolkiah, and the seat of the Brunei government. The palace is located on a leafy, riverside sprawl of hills on the banks of the Brunei River, a few kilometres southwest of Bandar Seri Begawan, Brunei's capital city. The palace is often at the centre of state occasions and royal hospitality.

landmarks.name: Kampong Ayer
landmarks.writeup: A historic water village built on stilts over the Brunei River.

wiki.extract: Kampung Ayer is a prominent traditional settlement in Bandar Seri Begawan, the capital of Brunei. It comprises neighbourhoods of traditional houses, schools and mosques built on stilts above the Brunei River near the capital's city centre. It has an area of about 10 square kilometres (3.9 sq mi); the total population was 10,250 in 2016. It has been historically nicknamed 'Venice of the East'.

cultural_events.name: Hari Raya Aidilfitri
cultural_events.writeup: A major Muslim festival marking the end of Ramadan, celebrated with prayers, feasts, and family gatherings.

wiki.extract: Eid al-Fitr is the first of the two main festivals in Islam, the other being Eid al-Adha. The holiday falls on the first day of Shawwal, the tenth month of the Islamic calendar. One of the most important Islamic celebrations, Eid al-Fitr is celebrated by Muslims worldwide as it marks the end of the month-long, dawn-to-dusk fasting (sawm) during Ramadan. The holiday is known under various other names in different languages and countries around the world.

cultural_events.name: Brunei National Day
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrated on February 23rd, commemorating Brunei's independence from British protection in 1984.

wiki.extract: National Day or Independence Day is the national day of Brunei, commemorating the anniversary of Brunei's proclamation of independence. It was made a national holiday by government decree in 1985. Although Brunei formally proclaimed independence from the United Kingdom on 1 January 1984, it did not celebrate its national day until 23 February.

food_writeup: Bruneian cuisine features a blend of Malay, Chinese, and Indian influences, with popular dishes including Nasi Lemak, Ambuyat (a sago starch dish), and Satay.
brief_history: Brunei was a powerful sultanate in the 15th and 16th centuries. It became a British protectorate in 1888 and gained full independence in 1984. The country is known for its wealth derived from extensive petroleum and natural gas fields.
